newsitem.title: ESTONIA: HANSA JUNE PROFIT 23.1 MLN KROONS.
newsitem.headline: HANSA JUNE PROFIT 23.1 MLN KROONS.

text.p: Estonia's leading bank Hansapank said on Thursday its June net profit was 23.1 million kroons compared to 41.8 million kroons in May.
Its half-year profit was 187.4 million kroons or 2.4 times higher than in the same period last year, it added in a statement.
The lower profit figure was because the bank started to make provisions on guarantees. During the month, provisions were made on the whole portfolio to the amount of 12.9 million kroons.
Its half-year profit figure was 73.2 percent of the forecast 256 million kroons for 1997.
The bank's total assets have grown by 37.5 percent during the year to 7.6 billion kroons at the end of June.
Liabilities rose by 1.8 billion kroons in six months. The main reasons behind the rapid growth were the 800 million kroons syndicated loan agreement and a rapid growth in deposits.
Deposits grew by 1.1 billion kroons or 32.3 percent in six months to 4.4 billion kroons.
Its loan portfolio stood at 4.26 billion kroons, a growth of 30.7 percent from the beginning of the year.
Shareholders' equity rose by 163.5 million kroons and stood at 863.5 million kroons.
Hansapank in June also received a 120 million kroons subordinated loan from EBRD, which was signed in May.

The banks' efficiency ratios for the first half-year were the following: ROE (return on equity) 47.5 percent, ROA (return on assets) 5.8 percent, net interest margin 5.5 percent and non-interest margin 3.14 percent.
The bank earned 410.8 million kroons in total revenues in six months, a rise of 68.7 percent compared to the same period last year.
Out of the total revenue, 37.3 percent was net interest income, 33.6 percent trading income and 26.3 percent fees and commissions and other items.
The largest expense item was personnel costs, which contributed 63.6 or 40.9 percent of total operating expenses. At the end of period, Hansapank employed 670 people.
